title: Sunny and the Possum Lantern | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the quokka spots a possum high in a tree holding a jar of fireflies that glow like a lantern, and watches the tiny lights drift free into the night sky. A peaceful story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories, perfect for sleepy little ones.
narration:
The bush had grown dark and hushed, and Sunny the little quokka was walking slowly along a familiar path. The trees stood tall on either side of her, their pale bark glowing faintly in the rising moonlight.

Something up in the branches caught her eye.

High up in the fork of a tall gum tree sat a possum — a small, round, grey possum with a long curling tail and enormous soft dark eyes. And in the possum's paws was something wonderful. A little glass jar. And inside the jar, fireflies were glowing.

Their light pulsed very slowly. On. Off. On. Off. Like tiny, gentle heartbeats, sending soft flickers of amber light through the dark branches above.

Sunny sat down at the base of the tree and watched from below. She did not call up or wave. She just watched. The possum looked down at her and blinked its wide eyes. And together, the two of them simply rested with the glowing jar between them, though they were quite far apart.

For a long while, the fireflies pulsed their soft light in the dark.

Then the possum, very carefully, very gently, set the jar on a wide flat branch and tipped it slowly to one side. One by one, the fireflies drifted out into the open air.

They rose without any hurry, blinking softly as they went — up through the branches, through the leaves, out into the wide open sky — until their tiny lights scattered among the stars, and Sunny could no longer tell which were fireflies and which were stars at all.

She lay back on the soft ground and let her eyes rest on the sky.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, fireflies. Goodnight, little one.
